title: Acids, Bases, and pH
hook: The pH scale measures how acidic or basic a solution is — and living cells must keep it within a narrow range to survive.
key_points: pH measures the concentration of hydrogen ions in a solution.
The scale runs from 0 (most acidic) to 14 (most basic), with 7 as neutral.
Acids release hydrogen ions; bases accept them or release hydroxide ions.
The scale is logarithmic: each step is a tenfold change in acidity.
Cells use buffers to hold pH steady, because enzymes only work in a narrow range.
content_html: The pH scale tells you how acidic or basic a watery solution is, based on how many hydrogen ions are floating around in it. It runs from 0 to 14: low numbers are acidic, high numbers are basic, and 7 — the pH of pure water — is neutral. Acids dump extra hydrogen ions into solution, while bases soak them up. For living things, this balance is not optional.
extra_html: The scale is logarithmic, meaning each whole-number step represents a tenfold change in hydrogen-ion concentration: a pH of 5 is ten times more acidic than 6, and a hundred times more acidic than 7. That sensitivity matters because the proteins and enzymes that drive a cell's chemistry only fold and function within a narrow pH range. Human blood, for instance, is held tightly near pH 7.4. To resist swings, cells and bodies rely on buffers — chemical pairs that absorb or release hydrogen ions to keep pH steady. Khan Academy's article on acids, bases, pH, and buffers explains how these systems protect life's chemistry.

related.title: Water and Life
related.hook: Life is built around a single small molecule — water. Its odd properties make it the stage on which almost all of biology happens.

related.title: The Molecules of Life
related.hook: Almost everything in a living cell is built from just four families of large molecules — carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids.

flashcards.prompt: What does pH measure, and what is the neutral value?
flashcards.back_html: pH measures the concentration of hydrogen ions in a solution. A value of 7 is neutral; below 7 is acidic, above 7 is basic.

flashcards.prompt: A solution of pH 4 is how much more acidic than a solution of pH 6?
flashcards.explanation_html: The pH scale is logarithmic, so each unit is a tenfold change. Two units (6 to 4) means 10 × 10 = 100 times more acidic.

flashcards.prompt: Why is keeping pH stable so important for cells?

choices.text: Enzymes only function within a narrow pH range
Cells need acidity to glow in the dark

flashcards.explanation_html: Most enzymes — the proteins that run a cell's chemistry — only work properly within a narrow pH window, so cells use buffers to hold it steady.
